result: WebDriver cannot currently simulate IME input well enough for composition-script testing.
Input Events tests need real user interaction; JS-only events and WebDriver contenteditable selection are weak.
CDP has Chromium-only input and IME hooks; useful for scoped Chromium proof, not raw device proof.
Appium Unicode input is special-path text insertion and does not prove native keyboard business logic.
Appium `mobile: performEditorAction` proves focused editor action dispatch, not composition lifecycle.
Android custom IME can drive `InputConnection` composing text, committed text, surrounding-text deletion, and selection-update callbacks.
Contenteditable catalog records specific OS/browser/IME scenarios and unknowns for a future matrix.
ProseMirror Android discussion shows keyboard/browser/version variation and supports device-matrix claim width.
